SHORT.Finding: **SPEC'D 2026-09-03, awaiting operator pick (operator: "the chords shown under the circle of fifths have been a surprisingly nice tool for me to write progressions before using compose tab. what is the pattern here we can enable?")**. Pattern named: **audition-first composing** - the Studio's chords-in-key strip is a PALETTE (zero commitment per tap, 7 chips all correct by construction, auditioned against a live key, circle co-present) where Compose is a CANVAS (commit-first). The gap: `renderChordChips()` plays the tap and DISCARDS it, so an ordered by-ear chord sequence - real creative output - is lost and re-entered by hand. Proposal, ranked: (1) **tap-trail capture** - remember the last N taps, offer "Keep these N -> Compose" via the existing seedKey bridge, trail clears on key change/close; (2) **name the pattern** - match the trail against songwriting-coach's proven families via `Circle.romanFor` and say "that is the Axis loop" + offer the canonical completion (teaches while he plays); (3) next-chord emphasis on the strip, **emphasis ONLY, never reordering** (the strip's calm comes from the 7 chips never moving - ux-coach recognition-over-recall); (4) audition-vs-commit mode in Compose = operator vision call, not assumed. Recommend building 1+2 as one feature. Full analysis: [design-audition-first-composing-20260903.md](design-audition-first-composing-20260903.md)

The finding that shaped it: `Export all skills` and `Export agent bundle` called the IDENTICAL downloadBundle under two names in two sections - the confusion was the presentation, not the bundle (which already carried AGENTS.md, capabilities.json and the full backup envelope offline). The AI Agent section is now a plain #agentBlock div ADOPTED into the Skills pane per render - deliberately outside the .accSec scan, since Accordion.init collects sections at init time and a section removed afterwards leaves a stale entry on a detached node. **ROOT-CAUSED + FIXED 2026-09-03 (PR #342, v342-12); TWO SCENARIOS AWAIT AN OPERATOR CALL.** Found by regressing the CE3 cold-start scenario, but the blast radius is far wider than the tour: after ANY row-tap play - the app's most common action - a 245px position:fixed z-96 iframe stayed pinned at y=58 across every tab, so the top ~300px of the library, Compose and Tune silently ate taps. Measured: elementFromPoint over a Compose progression pick returned IFRAME. Cause: `vidopen` means "the video is in THEATER", and nothing cleared it when the player minimized, so the CSS guard `.bt-player.mini:not(.vidopen) .bt-st-media:not(.min){max-height:0}` never matched. setVid's own stash comment had said since round 11 that "minimizeStudio demotes theater->PIP" - no code ever did it. Fix: minimizeStudio calls `_setVid('pip', true)` when a theater is up (fromOpen=true, so it does not overwrite the remembered choice). Verified: PIP docks at y=655/110px/z-95, Compose picks tappable again, iframe still mounted so audio survives, first-session.json green. A placement-only fix was considered and rejected: any LARGE visible video on a mini player overlays page content by construction - PIP is the only state that keeps it visible, skippable and off the page. **OPEN:** video-adlikely and video-pip pin the pre-fix contract (theater-on-mini) and are EXPECTED RED. Their asserts were deliberately NOT bent to agree - re-authoring ~45 steps of that choreography changes a contract the operator owns. If he prefers theater to stay, revert the one _setVid line.

**SHIPPED 2026-09-03 (PR #342, v342-11, operator UAT batch 6: "styles seem corrupted? or?").** The phone rendered v342-10 markup with v342-9 CSS and the stamp read v342-9 - a Frankenstein build, not an ordinary stale cache. Root cause: every asset was referenced by a BARE path, and HTTP/CDN caches key on URL - index.html revalidates, a URL that never changes never does. The sw.js CACHE bump was irrelevant (the SW is network-first and was never the culprit). Worst part: build-stamp.js is itself one of those assets, so the STAMP - the repo's documented "which build am I on" handle - reported the OLD version while newer HTML ran. The version oracle lied, which is why several UAT rounds this session judged a build that was not the build under test. Fix: one SSOT (build-stamp VERSION) drives a ?v= on every local asset URL via scripts/stamp-asset-versions.py, so new HTML can never pair with old assets; sw.js gains ignoreSearch so the unversioned precache still answers offline. Gated in the same commit by test/asset-version-lint.test.js + a third leg in check-cache-bump.sh. Evidence: 70/70 node files green, gate mutation-proven RED against the exact author mistake (bump the version, forget to re-stamp), live render shows zero 4xx on any versioned asset and the stamp reporting v342-11.

**SPEC'D 2026-09-03, awaiting operator answers (operator UAT batch 6: "can't we merge skills and agent accordion... the skills export needs to act as standalone zip file... should describe itself without any additional prompting just by uploading the zip").** Two accordions serve one job, and the job leaks across both - two exports, two mental models, and a Copy-starter-prompt step that is itself the tell that the bundle was not self-describing. Docs are fetched from public URLs, so a bundle handed to an offline agent is inert. Target: one accordion, one export, one import, ZERO prompt characters typed. The zip IS the interface - README.md + bundled AGENTS.md/capabilities.json + profile.json + skills/ + data/ + UPDATE.md, with one round-trip format serving all three update cases the operator named (one competency +1, porting external skills in, a fresh install corrected by a coaching session). Instructions stay viewable as a disclosure, never a step. Spec: docs/plans/design-skills-agent-merge-20260903.md. Two open questions for the operator (accordion name; whether data/ belongs in the skills zip or stays in Backup).

**SHIPPED 2026-09-03 (PR #342, v342-10, operator UAT batch 5: "too cluttered w text. simplicity FTW. UI standard layout? for export etc buttons, min prose").** There was no action-row convention, so six rows doing the same job had been invented at their own call sites in FOUR looks - a bordered .setRow card with a stacked description, an .aboutLink with an icon and a wrapping sentence, a .btn.ghost pair, and a raw URL as body text. The standard is now written in component-conventions.md ("Action rows": ONE ROW = ONE ACTION, verb-first label on one nowrap line, no per-row description, at most one caption per group, .saMeta for live state only, external rows take --brass ink + the leave-app glyph) and implemented as the single .setAction primitive; the four lookalike CSS rules were DELETED rather than left dormant, since a dead lookalike is what the next author reuses. Per machine-ssot-enforcement the gate ships in the same commit: test/settings-action-row-lint.test.js fails on a description inside an action row, on stacked captions, on a reintroduced lookalike class or rule, and on a URL rendered as body text. Evidence: 69/69 node files green, settings-action-rows scenario PASS and mutation-proven RED twice (ghost button restored, nowrap guard removed), the lint mutation-proven RED catching all three defects at once, settings-agent + settings-accordion-affordance + settings-skills-uat green after being repointed off the retired classes, live 412x915 both themes - five uniform 48px rows, zero clipped labels, zero console errors.

Each is a grouped card with a 10px gap now (the mobile settings convention, iOS and Material both), the header row is 52px, and the handle is a stroke chevron drawn from borders rather than a filled U+25BE, which is a desktop select glyph. **SHIPPED 2026-09-02 (PR #342, v342-6, operator UAT: "can we detect not playing anything -> playing (first load or idle time) and show the yt video - most likely to have ads. not between every song tho")**: the video shows itself exactly where a pre-roll is likely - an AD-LIKELY open (nothing was playing AND first-play-this-load, or the last stop was over VID_IDLE_MS=10min ago) opens the theater; every other open CARRIES the state the user left it in, so the video never jumps up between songs and is never yanked away (round 16 stands). Ad-likely BEATS a stale stored pref - the operator has twice asked to SEE the video when ads are likely. The rule is a PURE predicate `TracksModel.adLikelyOpen({wasPlaying, hasPlayedThisLoad, lastStopAt, now, idleMs})`, behaviour-tested across all four states + both idle boundaries (a scenario could not discriminate it: on a fresh device the round-16 fallback is also 'theater', so the browser test passed under a forced adLikely=false - extracting the seam is what made the rule provable). Mid-session carry proven on pixels in video-adlikely.json. VID_IDLE_MS is a judgment call, not measured - one named constant to tune

**SHIPPED 2026-09-02 (PR #342, v342-5, operator UAT: "don't auto hide yt video. I keep having to open it to skip after ads")**: THE APP NEVER HIDES THE VIDEO ON ITS OWN. Part 3 (disable incompatible) is n/a: over a diatonic key all four scale choices are playable (major/minor pentatonic interplay is a feature, not an incompatibility), so nothing to disable. **EXTENDED (PR #198)**: (a) the default is now PROGRESSION-AWARE - `Tracks.inferSoloDefault(key,mode,seq)` reads the actual chords via `Circle.romanFor` and upgrades the default to Mixolydian (a bVII-major tell over a major key) or Dorian (a major-IV tell over a minor key), else the safe pentatonic. **A note/chord spelled with a SHARP contradicts the degree label the same UI shows (music-theory-coach REJECT).** Building C-F-A# in C major, the third chord shows "A#" under a "bVII" roman-numeral label. Music-theory-coach verdict: over a stated key, spelling is FUNCTION-driven - the bVII is the lowered 7th (B lowered = **Bb**), and "A#" names a raised 6th (#6), the WRONG function. Showing "A#" while labeling it "bVII" is internally self-contradictory (numeral says flat-7, note says sharp-6). Coach REJECTS whenever the UI asserts a key/degree function; sharp spelling is acceptable ONLY in a keyless/chromatic context. This is the FORK-4 canonical-sharp limitation - the fix is key-aware spelling, which is exactly what the stalled linchpin **#98** (`spellScaleKeyAware`/`keyLabel`) delivers. Operator (2026-07-10) AUTHORIZED removing FORK-4 -> key-aware, confirming it is deterministic. **CORE BUILT + PROVEN (PR #198)**: `Circle.spellScaleKeyAware(root,mode)` + `Circle.spellRootInKey(keyRoot,keyMode,noteRoot)` - deterministic letter-per-degree spelling (each of A-G once, accidental to hit each pitch). 14 passing unit tests (`test/key-spelling.test.js`): F major -> Bb (not A#), bVII of C -> Bb, the note name now AGREES with the degree label. REMAINING (the staged wiring = the real FORK-4 removal): (1) route the render paths (chord names, scale note list, fretboard) through the key-aware spellers instead of `spell()`/`spellScale()`; (2) the picker offers SHARP-only key names (A#, D#, G#), and those keys spell to double-sharps under correct theory - so the removal also needs the picker to name flat keys with FLAT letters (Bb not A#). That picker change is a scope/UX call (operator owns). Supersedes the #98 approach with a tested core.
